input.title: Recursion Workshop
input.description: Sample course. Trace a recursive call from its first argument to the final return.
outcomes: Trace the order of returns through a call stack.

modules.title: The call stack
modules.description: Build a mental model for what waits and what returns.

lessons.title: Why the base case matters
lessons.summary: Read a countdown from its last call back to the first.
objectives: Name the call that returns first.
Explain what the waiting calls retain.
lessons.reading: For countdown(2), the calls start at 2, 1 and then 0. The base case at 0 returns with no new call. The call at 1 resumes and returns. The call at 2 finishes last.

exercise.prompt: Write the call order and the return order for countdown(2).

modules.title: Folder trees
modules.description: Apply the same idea when a call has two branches.

lessons.title: Walk a folder tree
lessons.summary: Trace the return from each folder to its parent.
lessons.reading: Visit the first child folder, return to the parent, and then visit the second child. A folder without child folders returns after visiting its own files.

cards.front: What happens to a call while its recursive call runs?
cards.back: It waits at the call site with its own local variables.
A branch that returns without making another recursive call.

document.title: Countdown trace
document.content:
Sample trace, Recursion Workshop
Calls: 2 → 1 → 0
Returns: 0 → 1 → 2
At 0, the base case returns without another call.

operations.body: Sample discussion prompt: When would the two orders stop looking like reverses?

operations.answer: Sample submission entered by the course owner for demonstration. Calls: 2, 1, 0. Returns: 0, 1, 2. The call at 0 is the base case.

learner.answer: Calls: 2, 1, 0. Returns: 0, 1, 2. The call at 0 is the base case.
